items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: Jerry was so old until the hair was off his back. He used to shed the hair off his back sliding in and out of them holes... Jerry would know and Jerry would walk down the hall besides you... Nobody was scared of him.

ctx.x: That's right, he wrote for them and, of course, Donald Kirkpatrick, the piano player in the band, was a wonderful, wonderful arranger. He come in after Horace Henderson left. And he used to write for Chick Webb, too, and so he made a lot of arrangements for Don, beautiful arrangements. And sometimes Jerry Blake would play baritone. Other than that he'd play alto because we didn't use two tenors then. We used three altos. And then when Don would play alto, the lead alto, then Jerry Blake would play the tenor part,…

Sometimes he'd use a combination like soprano on top and the two altos and the tenor and the baritone. The baritone would play a lot of times what the bass clarinet would play today. They would write it that way, too, like sometimes there'd be soprano on top and then three clarinets, you see, and then the baritone on the bottom, and Jerry would play a kind of subtone effect so it would blend with the clarinets, you see.
